_readme: Author-confirmed facts for scripts/check-content.mjs. Each fact is what YOUR book and notes say. require = notes must still state it; forbid = text that must not appear (distractor choices are ignored); numeric = every captured number must be in allowed. computed = worked examples recomputed by the script. Add a fact when you confirm one; change a value only after checking your book. answerKeys = the exact text of the correct choice for each question the author has verified against the book's answer key (position-independent, so shuffling cannot break it). Any question in pinChapters without a pin is reported until someone verifies it.

facts.statement: Class A 1 to 126, Class B 128 to 191, Class C 192 to 223

forbid.reason: Class A ends at 126; 127 is loopback

facts.statement: EUI-64 inserts FF:FE in the middle of the MAC and inverts the 7th bit
facts.source: Chapter 7 notes (the original note text said FF:FF, corrected)

facts.statement: Link-local FE80::/10, unique local FC00::/7, loopback ::1
IPv6 is 128 bits, 96 more than IPv4
Administrative distance: connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, IGRP 100, OSPF 110, RIP 120
facts.source: Chapters 9 and 10 notes and review answer keys

facts.statement: External EIGRP AD 170; unknown source AD 255 is never used; the router checks AD first when two updates list the same network
facts.source: Sybex chapter 11 slide deck, slide 6 (Administrative Distance)

facts.statement: SNMP traps use UDP 162; polling (GET) uses UDP 161; traps are unacknowledged, INFORMs are acknowledged
facts.source: Author's real-world note on SNMP traps

facts.statement: RIP: 15 hops maximum, 16 is unreachable, updates every 30 seconds, RIPv2 multicast 224.0.0.9
facts.source: Chapter 10 notes and review answer key

facts.statement: RIP is distance-vector, OSPF is link-state (Dijkstra), EIGRP is hybrid, BGP is path-vector
facts.source: Chapter 10 notes and review answer key

forbid.reason: EIGRP is hybrid (distance-vector with link-state behavior)
book Q12: TTL expiry alone does not prove a routing loop
book Q2: routers in one AS do not necessarily use the same routing protocol

facts.statement: EtherType 0x0800 IPv4 and 0x0806 ARP; FCS is 4 bytes
Route selection: longest prefix, then lowest AD, then lowest metric
The host ARP cache command is arp -a (the book prints arp -g)
facts.source: Chapter 9 notes and review answer key

facts.statement: 802.1Q tag is 4 bytes: 16-bit TPID 0x8100, 3-bit CoS, 1-bit DEI, 12-bit VLAN ID
STP is 802.1D, RSTP is 802.1w; default port state is blocking; convergence takes 50 seconds
VLANs 1 and 1002 to 1005 cannot be deleted
802.3at delivers 25.5 watts
A switch learns from the SOURCE MAC and forwards by the DESTINATION MAC

forbid.reason: switches learn from the source MAC

facts.statement: Default masks: Class A 255.0.0.0, Class B 255.255.0.0, Class C 255.255.255.0
Hosts per subnet is 2^h - 2; subnets 2^s; block size 256 minus the mask value

forbid.reason: hosts per subnet need the minus 2

facts.statement: A /30 (255.255.255.252) fits point-to-point WAN links; a /24 wastes 252 addresses per link

forbid.reason: the chapter recommends /30 for WAN links

facts.statement: NAT overloading is port address translation (PAT)
Split horizon: a router does not advertise a route back out the interface it learned it on
facts.source: Chapter 10 notes (added with the split horizon section; confirm against the book)

forbid.reason: split horizon applies only to the interface the route was learned on

facts.statement: OSI layers 1 to 7: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
require: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away
All People Seem To Need Data Processing

facts.statement: DoD Host-to-Host = Transport, Internet = Network, Network Access = Data Link + Physical

forbid.reason: the DoD Internet layer maps to OSI Network, not Transport

facts.statement: Router to hub uses straight-through (MDI to MDI-X); switch to hub uses crossover
facts.source: MDI/MDI-X rule (Professor Messer N10-008 2.3); corrects the whiteboard layer shortcut

facts.statement: Routing (router or Layer 3 switch) rewrites both MACs and decrements TTL; source and destination IP stay the same without NAT. Layer 2 switching changes none of them.

forbid.reason: a Layer 2 switch does not touch the TTL
routing does not change IP addresses (NAT does)

facts.statement: Inter-VLAN routing on a Cisco Layer 3 switch needs an SVI per VLAN and the ip routing command
TCP three-way handshake is SYN, SYN/ACK, ACK; graceful close is FIN, ACK, FIN, ACK
Well-known 0-1023, registered 1024-49151, dynamic 49152-65535
HTTP is TCP 80 and HTTPS is TCP 443
ARP poisoning changes IP-to-MAC bindings; copying a presented MAC alone is not sufficient.
facts.source: Cisco DAI guide, ARP Poisoning; docs/network-plus-ch21-verification.md

forbid.reason: Interface MAC spoofing alone does not establish false ARP bindings.

facts.statement: A CCFL-backlit LCD uses an inverter; LED-backlit LCDs use LED-driver circuitry and OLED has no separate backlight.
facts.source: Analog Devices MAX8722C CCFL inverter documentation (https://www.analog.com/en/products/max8722c.html); Texas Instruments TPS68000 LED backlight driver (https://www.ti.com/product/TPS68000); manufacturer model guide required for service.

facts.statement: Adapter compatibility depends on model-supported voltage, connector or PD profile, cable and device requirements; wattage alone is insufficient.
facts.source: USB-IF USB Power Delivery overview https://www.usb.org/usb-charger-pd; Apple Power Adapter guide https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509; HP power adapter guidance https://support.hp.com/us-en/document/ish_2025983-1502949-16.

forbid.reason: Compatibility depends on electrical and product requirements, not wattage alone.

facts.statement: Bluetooth PAN support and some mobile operating systems support tethering over Bluetooth; it is platform and service dependent.
facts.source: Bluetooth SIG Personal Area Networking Profile 1.0 https://www.bluetooth.com/specifications/specs/personal-area-networking-profile-1-0/; Apple iPhone Personal Hotspot guide https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/share-your-internet-connection-iph45447ca6/27/ios/27.
require: supported Bluetooth tethering can share internet
Do not claim Bluetooth can never tether

facts.statement: WPA2-Personal commonly pairs a shared passphrase with AES-CCMP; WPA3-Personal uses SAE; advertised PHY rates are not guaranteed client throughput.
facts.source: Wi-Fi Alliance WPA3 announcement https://www.globenewswire.com/fr/news-release/2018/06/26/1529297/0/en/wi-fi-alliance-introduces-wi-fi-certified-wpa3-security.html; Microsoft WLAN authentication/cipher schema https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/nativewifi/wlan-profileschema-authencryption-security-element; Intel Wi-Fi throughput guide https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000059666/wireless.html.
require: PHY/link rate is not application throughput

forbid.reason: WPA2 and WPA3 identify distinct authentication/security modes.
